cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: The Logic Gets Bigger
cards.instruction: Use every new detail to expand the impossible system, its history, and the consequences of breaking it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Our meeting chairs float at noon. Book the ceiling; they've had landing rights since the first furniture strike.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we stand and tie the chairs down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Restraint broke the last treaty. That's when the desks joined them. We'll need an airspace permit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker only issues floor permits.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then promote her to altitude minister before the cabinets claim the roof.

mechanism: A treats its pupil office setup shortcuts as failures to remember furniture history, extending the floating-chair system into treaties and higher jurisdiction.
confusable: Not just inventing a rule to win one request: each response enlarges a connected system with past conflict and future consequences.
comparison: Meeting furniture governance versus dinner crockery diplomacy.
